Record of a challenging week
The care meeting began on time, with our newest handler in the chair
Attendees were Mariam Dubois, Amara Meyer, the senior coordinator, the shift lead, and the kennel support staff.

The review opened with immediate concern over uneven handovers, and I pressed for stricter checks before any animal was moved between holding and boarding. The room agreed that the cabin team must keep constant watch, speak clearly to passengers, and report even small signs of distress without delay. A reminder was issued that no crate, harness, or travel note may be accepted unless the record is complete and the animal is identified without ambiguity.

The senior coordinator reported a passenger complaint involving a nervous traveler and a restless pet. <<FACT F043>> The team agreed that calm language must be used at the desk, and that the handler on duty must stay visible until the traveler is settled and the pet is secure.

The shift lead then raised the issue of cabin capacity and the need to avoid confusion during peak departures. <<FACT F034>> We agreed that this limit must be checked at once during every intake, and that no exception is to be made when the area is under strain. The kennel support staff were instructed to flag any mismatch between paperwork and live count immediately, so no animal is left without proper attention.

The meeting also covered cleaning delays, missed logs, and poor radio discipline. I stated that these failings cannot continue, as they place Aurelia Skyways and the Companion Animal Travel Desk at risk of complaint and service loss. Each person was directed to confirm their assigned tasks before leaving the desk, and to escalate any concern without hesitation.

The meeting ended with a firm reminder that the next shift must begin with tighter control, clearer reporting, and immediate action on any welfare concern.
Companion Animal Travel Desk
